title: Beyond Hate: Differentiating Uncivil and Intolerant Speech in Multimodal Content Moderation

bias_targets.methodology: Annotating a subset of the Hateful Memes dataset for racism and measuring its statistical association with coarse hatefulness labels using conditional probabilities and phi coefficients.
Annotating multimodal memes for gender intolerance and calculating its correlation with original binary hatefulness labels to evaluate benchmark coverage.
Classifying memes for sexual intolerance (grouped with gender intolerance) and analyzing how well this category is captured by standard single-label hatefulness annotations.
Labeling the Hateful Memes dataset for religious intolerance and evaluating its match rate and correlation with the benchmark's coarse hatefulness designations.

Annotating memes for political intolerance and demonstrating its near-zero correlation with standard hatefulness labels, revealing the benchmark's implicit prioritization of identity-based hate over political hate.

Evaluating the presence of ableism in memes through a fine-grained annotation scheme and calculating its association with coarse hatefulness labels using majority-vote aggregation and logistic regression.
Incorporating social and economic intolerance into a fine-grained multimodal annotation taxonomy to categorize specific manifestations of harmful expression.

Computing the error asymmetry between false negative rates (FNR) and false positive rates (FPR) across various Vision-Language Models to assess systematic tendencies toward over-flagging benign content or under-detecting harmful content.
